heroHeadline: ARTEMIS III CREW REVEAL IN 2 DAYS (JUNE 9, JSC) — FINAL SRB SEGMENTS APPROACHING KSC BY RAIL; CREW DAY 58; BLUE ORIGIN RTF YEAR-END 2026 TARGET; IFT-12 INVESTIGATION ONGOING
heroSubtitle: June 7: The Artemis III crew announcement is 2 days away (June 9, 11 a.m. EDT, Johnson Space Center, NASA+/YouTube), when the four astronauts assigned to the redesignated Earth-orbit rendezvous and docking test mission (targeting late 2027) will be publicly named for the first time. Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex is hosting a public watch party coinciding with the livestream. On the hardware front, the final 8 Artemis III SLS five-segment solid rocket booster segments, which departed Northrop Grumman's Utah railyard facility on June 2 via Union Pacific rail, are approaching KSC and expected to arrive June 8–11 for summer stacking alongside the SLS core stage (in the VAB since April 28). Marshall Space Flight Center continues fabricating the Artemis III structural spacer barrel and rings. The Artemis II crew — Commander Reid Wiseman, Pilot Victor Glover, Mission Specialist Christina Koch, and Canadian Mission Specialist Jeremy Hansen — are on Day 58 post-splashdown at Johnson Space Center, continuing physiological reconditioning. The Artemis II Orion capsule is in de-servicing at KSC's Multi-Payload Processing Facility; the heat shield is scheduled for shipment to Marshall this summer for X-ray scans and Avcoat sample extractions. Blue Origin CEO Dave Limp (June 3) is targeting return-to-flight for New Glenn before year-end 2026 using an 'alternative vertical conops' — bypassing full reconstruction of the destroyed transporter-erector. The propellant farm (LOX/LH2/LNG tanks) and water tower at LC-36 survived the May 29 explosion intact, removing long-lead infrastructure replacement from the critical path. Moon Base I fall 2026 delivery remains on hold pending New Glenn return-to-flight. The FAA's mishap investigation into Starship IFT-12's Booster 19 boostback burn failure (May 22) is ongoing — IFT-13 blocked from a flight license, return-to-flight projected no earlier than July–August 2026. The orbital propellant transfer demonstration (mandatory Artemis III HLS qualification milestone) has slipped to Q3-Q4 2026. House Appropriations markup (May 13) recommends $24.438B for NASA — flat with FY2026, rejecting the White House's 23% cut. Artemis Accords: 67 signatories. CLPS 2.0 RFP responses due June 30.
